notes.content:
Work done 2026-08-11 (NOT closing — leaving the close decision to the maintainer).

todo!() removed. marviken_tests.rs rewritten: 6 active tests, none ignored, whole file runs in 1.39-1.44 s measured in release mode, so nothing is #[ignore]d. Full crate lib suite after the change: 940 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored (was 924/0/14).

Case setup verified against NUREG/CR-2671 rather than inherited. Corrections to the previous file: (a) the hard-coded 33 K subcooling is RIGHT for test 24 but WRONG for test 23, whose nominal subcooling is 3 K (Table 4:2 row 5, p.21/PDF 37) — the two tests differ by ~2.3x in measured flux at the same pressure because of it; (b) 500 mm and L/D = 0.3 are CONFIRMED (Table 3:1, p.7/PDF 23: D = 500 mm, L = 166 mm, converging only, rounded 250 mm-radius inlet, used in tests 23 and 24 only); (c) Fig 8:24 is CONFIRMED as the right figure, but it is report p.100 = PDF p.116, not PDF 113 — the offset is +16; (d) the previous code routed through calculate_velocity_mass_flowrate_and_state_in_cd_nozzle, which takes its choke from get_critical_pressure_ratio_pure_vapour, an ideal-gas pure-vapour critical pressure ratio meaningless for subcooled water; it now calls get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_multiphase_ph directly.

RESULT (measured, release, v0.2.5): test 23 VALIDATED (mean |dev| 12.6 %, signed +5.9 %, max 23.1 %, inside a justified +/-25 % / +/-15 % budget). Test 24 NOT VALIDATED (mean |dev| 48.6 %, signed -48.5 %, max 70.2 %, 31 of 40 points outside the band) and is kept as an explicitly-labelled characterisation whose assertions bracket the measured envelope. Tolerance derived from a measured error budget, not reverse-engineered: experimental scatter +/-12.9 %/+/-20.0 % (dominant), digitisation RMS 6.3 % vs Table 8:3 endpoints, numerics <0.001 %.

KEY FINDING, filed as bead op-dqng: the test-24 deficit is a solver branch-selection defect, not an HEM limitation. The bare HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion, built in the same test file from the crate's public (p,s) flashes with no heuristics, reproduces test 24 to a mean 9.0 % with a -1.8 % signed bias. The dispatcher instead takes the bubble-point sonic kink because quality-at-energy-max < 0.03 and DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0 is not reached at 33 K — the documented 'overlap zone'. Marviken settles it in favour of the energy-balance branch. Deliberately not fixed here (that would be fitting the model to its own validation data).

Docs updated in the same change: crate README (two Marviken passages), docs/notes.md, docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md line 81, and the crate CLAUDE.md Marviken section + ignored-test table + suite counts — the bead's own staleness comment about CLAUDE.md is therefore addressed. Also filed: op-2umf (CATALOGUE.md missing the nrc1982marviken entry), op-sxoa (Table 4:2 row 7 OCR-truncated for tests 23/24). op-ja3t commented and can be unblocked.

description: Part of op-72hy. crate::repository::save_repository / crate::advanced_git::save (crates/kovan/src/repository.rs, advanced_git.rs -- already wired to a UI button per op-nswf) must abstract submodule mechanics from the user per the comment: when private literature has changed, (1) commit the private literature submodule repo FIRST, (2) stage the resulting new submodule commit pointer in the parent repo, (3) commit the parent. If step (1) fails, KOVAN must NOT proceed to create a parent commit referencing an invalid/uncommitted submodule state -- the whole Save Repository action for that changeset must abort/report the failure instead. Depends on op-xq8t (needs the submodule config to exist) and op-dlv8 (needs to know which papers are PrivateSubmodule-mode so it knows what belongs in the private repo's own changeset).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented in crates/kovan/src/repository.rs: save_repository() now commits the private submodule FIRST via save_private_submodule() (its own tree-build + diff + commit, scoped to root.restricted_sources_dir()'s own .git, sharing the parent's tree-building/commit machinery via new shared helpers build_tree_from()/commit_tree()) whenever root.private_submodule_ready(). Any error there propagates via ? before the parent repo is touched at all -- the hard atomicity requirement is satisfied structurally by Rust's own early-return, no explicit rollback needed since nothing on the parent side has been written yet. The parent tree then records the submodule's current commit as a single gitlink entry (mode 0o160000/tree::EntryKind::Commit, via a new SubmoduleGitlink type) instead of walking its contents -- confirmed by test to actually be Commit-mode, not Tree-mode. .gitmodules is written/refreshed so real git submodule tooling recognises the same repository. status() gained the same gitlink preview via a read-only private_submodule_head() (documented gap: it previews the submodule's last COMMIT, not an uncommitted in-flight worktree change inside it, to keep status() genuinely non-writing). When no submodule is configured or not ready (checked via KovanRoot::private_submodule_ready(), added under op-xq8t), behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before this bead -- restricted_sources_dir() fully excluded, no gitlink, no .gitmodules touch. 5 new tests (gitlink-recorded, gitlink-bumps-on-change, unready-falls-back, submodule-open-failure-leaves-parent-untouched, status-stays-read-only). Verified: cargo check -p kovan --all-targets --all-features clean; cargo test -p kovan --lib --release: 370 passed (was 365), 0 failed, including all 7 pre-existing repository tests unchanged.

title: Save Repository: submodule-aware, atomic-ish save sequencing

design:
Five corrections to `htgr_sim_v1` raised by the maintainer (email, 2026-09-07),
verified against the code before filing.

**The headline finding: two of the five are the schematic misrepresenting
physics that is already correct.** For an educational simulator that is
arguably worse than a physics bug — a reader learns the wrong thing from the
picture while the numbers underneath are right, and nothing in the output
contradicts them.

## The five items, with what the code actually does

### 1. Helium flow in the core should show top to bottom — **DRAWING ONLY**

**The physics is already correct.** `physics/primary_loop.rs:5`:

> *"helium is delivered to the **top** of the core, flows **downward** through
> the ..."*

and cold helium rises through the side-reflector channels
(`primary_loop.rs:20`, `:55` — "the published cold-helium-rises-in-the-
reflector" arrangement).

So the model has downward core flow with upward reflector return, which is the
HTR-10 arrangement. **The schematic draws it wrongly or ambiguously.** Fix is in
`app/schematic.rs`.

### 2. Pebble drop and discharge for refuelling — **PARTLY PRESENT, NO DYNAMICS**

The **discharge-tube geometry exists**:
`physics/reactor_model/htr10_rz_geometry.rs` carries the conus and discharge
tube (benchmark zone 6, `r = [0, 25]` cm), a dummy-pebble-only region, and the
carbon brick outside the discharge tube. `:252` already notes the composition
varies "over the fuel cycle as pebbles are added and discharged".

**What is missing is the circulation itself** — no pebble drop, no discharge, no
recirculation, no burnup-dependent routing. This is a **new feature**, not a
correction, and it is on-line refuelling, which is the defining operational
characteristic of a pebble bed.

Scope question worth settling: is this wanted as a *schematic animation* only,
or as a *model* with pebble residence time and burnup? Those differ by an order
of magnitude in effort, and the second overlaps `op-jyyp`.

### 3. Purification system should be represented — **ABSENT ENTIRELY**

No match for purification, helium cleanup or coolant cleanup anywhere in the
example. Fully new.

The HTR-10 helium purification system removes H2O, CO, CO2, H2, N2/O2 and
particulates from a side stream. Same scope question as item 2: schematic box
and flow path, or an actual mass-balance model? A drawn box is cheap and
probably the right first step, but it should be labelled as representational.

### 4. Shift the steam generator lower — **LAYOUT ONLY**

Pure `app/schematic.rs` geometry.

Worth checking while there: the SG vessel sits *beside* the reactor vessel with
the circulator above it, per the module docs (`schematic.rs:687`, `:698`).
Lowering the SG should preserve that relative arrangement and the hot-gas-duct
cross-vessel connection.

### 5. Gas flow in the primary loop and helical SG should be counter-current — **DRAWING ONLY**

**The physics is already counter-current, and is defended by a test.**

- `physics/temperature_cross/lmtd_profile.rs:738` uses
  `FlowArrangement::CounterCurrent`
- `:148` — *"Pure single-pass counter-current is assumed, `F = 1`"*
- `physics/steam_generator.rs` has
  `counter_flow_index_map_is_its_own_inverse`, whose comment states the risk
  exactly:

  > *"This is the whole of the counter-flow arrangement — get it wrong and the
  > exchanger silently becomes co-current, which is a different (and worse)
  > machine that still runs and still produces plausible-looking numbers."*

So the model is right and guarded. **The schematic draws co-current.** Fix is in
`app/schematic.rs`.

## Suggested split

| item | where | kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1. core flow direction | `app/schematic.rs` | drawing correction |
| 5. counter-current SG/primary | `app/schematic.rs` | drawing correction |
| 4. SG vertical position | `app/schematic.rs` | layout |
| 2. pebble drop/discharge | schematic + possibly physics | **new feature** |
| 3. purification system | schematic + possibly physics | **new feature** |

**Items 1, 4 and 5 are one small schematic change and should go together.** They
are cheap, they are corrections rather than features, and 1 and 5 are actively
teaching the wrong thing today.

**Items 2 and 3 need a scope decision first** (representational drawing vs
modelled system) and should be separate beads once that is settled. Item 2 in
its modelled form belongs with `op-jyyp` (HTR-10 pebble-bed retarget) rather
than here.

## Acceptance

- Schematic shows downward core flow with the reflector return rising.
- Schematic shows counter-current gas/steam in the helical SG and primary loop.
- SG repositioned without breaking the vessel arrangement or duct connection.
- Any new schematic element added for items 2/3 is **labelled as
  representational** unless it is backed by a model, per the workspace rule
  against implying validation that does not exist.

## Note

Purely a GUI/schematic change for items 1, 4, 5, so the reference baseline
(`headless::tests::matches_the_recorded_reference_baseline`) must stay
**bit-exact**. If a schematic edit moves it, something has been changed that
should not have been.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: P0+P1 schematic rewrite done on branch htgr-sim-v1-schematic-htr10-primary-loop (not pushed, no PR per coordinator). - SG offset UPWARD per maintainer's authoritative #154 comment (was 'lower' in the issue body): reactor y230-630 (H=400), SG y138-546; SG bottom 84pt (0.21H) above reactor bottom, SG top 92pt (0.23H) above reactor top. Inverted steam_generator_sits_lower_than_the_reactor -> steam_generator_is_offset_upward_from_the_reactor. - Compact horizontal hot/cold duct bundle between the vessels, counter-flowing, replacing the rectangular over-the-top loop. - Reactor: upward cold-He chevrons in the side reflector, upper-plenum bracket, downward cue into the hot-gas plenum; NO graphics over the pebble bed. - SG-internal helium chevrons: centre UP, two coil channels DOWN, periphery UP; water/steam up-chevrons beside them = counter-current. - Moved the SG helical-coil hot-gas + feedwater nozzle stubs so primary helium is on the reactor-facing (left) side, water/steam on the turbine side (small shared-component edit in draw_helical_coil; widget_studio still builds). - Removed #[ignore] from the item-5 counter-current test, rewrote it to check flow through the coil region (the old nozzle-elevation check was measuring the wrong thing). Verification: cargo build --release --example htgr_sim_v1 clean; 139 example tests + 334 lib tests pass (all 12 schematic geometry tests, headless matches_the_recorded_reference_baseline bit-exact); headless stdout byte-identical before/after; no physics files touched. Follow-ups worth beads: (a) circulator sits high so the cold-He run drops ~430pt down the SG-vessel side to reach the bundle - a real topology feature but prominent; consider a lower circulator or a shorter drop. (b) items 2/3 (pebble discharge, He purification) deferred per coordinator - a real pebble-circulation model needs residence-time + burnup routing (overlaps op-jyyp); a real purification model needs a side-stream mass balance (H2O/CO/CO2/H2/N2 adsorption). Left bead OPEN for maintainer.
